citations.assessment: The passage gives Kohen and Yehoshua son of Rabbi Simon together in Levi’s name.
Ruth Rabbah gives Yehoshua of Sikhnin at the matching lemma. Preserve the paired names separately.
Esther Rabbah places Kohen in Azaryah’s name in the royal throne interpretation.
The passage names Kohen, Ḥizkiyah, Yaakov bar Aḥa and Ami walking together in Sepphoris.

Ruth Rabbah gives Yehoshua of Sikhnin at the matching lemma. Preserve the paired names separately.
Esther Rabbah places Kohen in Azaryah’s name in the royal throne interpretation.
The passage names Kohen, Ḥizkiyah, Yaakov bar Aḥa and Ami walking together in Sepphoris.
The printed chapter heading is correct. Shabbat gives Aḥa, Meyasha and Kohen together in the name of the rabbis of Caesarea. Do not narrow the chain to Meyasha alone.
The final Demai passage directly puts Kohen in the name of the rabbis of Caesarea.
The Shabbat chain directly names Aḥa and Meyasha together with Kohen, whereas Demai singles out Kohen.
